And Jesus answering saith unto them,
Have faith in God.
column6: Jesus tells us directly to trust God with everything in our lives. It means believing He is good and powerful, and that He cares for us deeply. We can lean on Him no matter what we face, knowing He is always there.
column7: What challenge or decision in your life today can you choose to fully trust God with?
column8: Take a moment to name one worry you have and consciously give it to God in prayer, trusting He will guide you.
column9: Jesus encourages us: "Trust God with everything."
column10: Dear God, thank you for being trustworthy and good. Please help me to truly have faith in You in every part of my life today. Amen.

column5: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
column6: When worries or anxieties pop up, this verse reminds us we don't have to carry them all by ourselves. We can gently hand every single one over to God, because He truly loves and cares deeply for you. He wants to share your burdens.
column7: What specific worry or anxious thought can you intentionally give to God today?
column8: Take a moment to pause, breathe, and consciously tell God about one specific worry that's on your mind right now, trusting Him with it.
column9: Give God your worries; He truly cares for you.
column10: Dear God, I'm feeling some worries right now. I choose to give them to You, knowing You care for me deeply. Please bring me Your peace.

column5:
Who
is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth
in mercy.
column6: Take a moment today to sit quietly with Micah 7:18. Let the words settle rather than reaching immediately for their meaning. Sometimes the most honest response to Scripture is simply to let it be present.
column7: What does this verse stir in you today — not what it means, but what it makes you feel?
column8: Read this verse once more slowly, and carry one word from it with you through the day.
column9: One word from Micah 7:18 — let it follow you today.
column10: Lord, I'm here with Your Word even when I don't have words of my own. Let that be enough today. Amen.
